source_text: Fateor tamen, nimis te cogitasse, quid diceres; et ingenium tuum apparet, et studium; solertissime prorsus quid asserendum esset pro peccati traduce ponderasti; nemo alter callidius scribere potuisset pro naturali malo; quod quidem nec tu ipse tam urbane implere potuisses, nisi ingenium tuum magistri veteris commenta iuvissent.
pass_a_gloss: I confess nevertheless that you thought too much what you would say; and your talent appears, and your zeal; most cleverly indeed you weighed what must be asserted for the tradux of sin; no other could have written more cunningly for natural evil; which indeed not even you yourself could have filled so urbanely, unless the inventions of an old master had helped your talent.

lemmas.lexica: LS tradux=vine-shoot/layer; Blaise tradux peccati=transmission of sin by descent
LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: I admit, however, that you thought very hard about what to say. Your talent and your effort are evident. You certainly weighed most skillfully what should be asserted on behalf of inherited sin. No one else could have written more cleverly for natural evil. Indeed, even you could not have accomplished it so elegantly had your old teacher’s inventions not helped your talent.

choices.why: Julian's polemic target is inherited sin as a natural evil (malum naturale), the vine-layer metaphor, not a later systematic 'original sin' slogan and not soul-traducianism as such.
rejected: original sin (later system as default gloss)
traducianism of the soul (not the load here)

choices.why: Julian's Manichaean charge: an evil that is a nature, not a will's act.
Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
